correctness.rationale: The same pinned RESULT.md defines G(t)=exp[-D(t-tau(1-e^-t/tau))], M_j(gamma)=integral t^j exp(-gamma t)G(t)dt and K_c=2/[(mu+beta_s gamma)M_0]. Its f_gamma has strictly concave log, and the hazard ratio S/f decreases strictly, implying E(T^2)<2E(T)^2, equivalently M_0 M_2<2M_1^2. Therefore h=M_0/M_1-gamma has h' <0 and h(0)>0, h(infinity)=0, with K_c' sign reversing once iff beta_s>beta_c=mu M_1(0)/M_0(0). Laplace expansion G(t)=1-Dt^2/(2tau)+O(t^3) yields h(gamma)=2D/(tau gamma)+O(gamma^-2), and inverse Taylor at h(0) yields both endpoint laws. Boundary beta_s=0 and gamma=0 are explicitly handled. This proof verifies the mathematics, not its priority.
